What a rating rests on

Source: R/accessors.R
rating_support.Rd

The stage ranges a rating rests on, and which of them are evidence and which are decision. There are five:

  • observed: the stage range of the gaugings (evidence of source type gauging), with how many there are;

  • modelled: the stage range of evidence that is not a measurement (a modelled value, a cross-section or structure computation, or a point read off another rating);

  • fitted: the stage range the equations are declared over, which can be wider than the evidence after extend_rating_low() or graft_rating();

  • operational: the range the rating may be used over, if stated (see set_operational_limits()); NA if not;

  • numerical: where the equations give a finite discharge. Beyond it apply_rating() fails.

apply_rating() uses the same ranges to say, for every stage it computes, how well supported that stage is (its support column).

With by = "limb" it gives instead how much of each limb rests on gaugings: how many fall inside it, the stage range they cover, and how far the limb extends beyond them at either end. A limb that stretches well past its highest gauging is an extrapolation there, whatever its fit statistics say.

Usage

rating_support(x, by = "range")

Arguments

x

A FlodeRating, FlodeSegmentedRating or FlodeRatingTable. A table holds equations only, so it has no observed or modelled range.

by

"range" (default) for the five ranges, or "limb" for the per-limb table. "limb" needs gaugings, so a FlodeRatingTable is refused.

Value

With by = "range", a data.table of five rows with range, lower_stage_m, upper_stage_m, n_evidence (gaugings or modelled points, NA for the ranges that are not evidence) and basis, a sentence on what the range is. A range that does not exist is NA.

With by = "limb", for a FlodeRating, one row per limb: limb, lower_stage_m, upper_stage_m, n_gaugings, gauged_min_stage_m, gauged_max_stage_m, lower_unsupported_m and upper_unsupported_m (how far the limb extends below its lowest and above its highest gauging, m), and the same as a fraction of the limb's width, lower_unsupported_frac and upper_unsupported_frac. A limb with no gaugings has n_gaugings 0 and NA elsewhere. For a FlodeSegmentedRating, one row with n_gaugings, gauged_min_stage_m and gauged_max_stage_m.

See also

apply_rating() for the support column; set_operational_limits(); flag_extrapolated_limbs(), which the support classes supersede; rating_evidence()

Examples

set.seed(1)
stage_m <- seq(0.5, 2.5, by = 0.05)
discharge_cms <- 5 * stage_m^1.6 + rnorm(length(stage_m), sd = 0.02)
fit <- rate_optimise(discharge_cms, stage_m)
rating_support(fit)
#>          range lower_stage_m upper_stage_m n_evidence
#>         <char>         <num>         <num>      <int>
#> 1:    observed           0.5    2.5000e+00         41
#> 2:    modelled            NA            NA          0
#> 3:      fitted           0.5    2.5000e+00         NA
#> 4: operational            NA            NA         NA
#> 5:   numerical          -Inf   1.3029e+192         NA
#>                                                                                                  basis
#>                                                                                                 <char>
#> 1:                                                         gaugings: evidence of source type 'gauging'
#> 2: evidence of any other source type (modelled, cross-section, structure equation, operational rating)
#> 3:                                                     the stage range the equations are declared over
#> 4:                                                            not stated; see set_operational_limits()
#> 5:                         where the equations give a finite discharge; beyond it apply_rating() fails
rating_support(fit, by = "limb")
#>     limb lower_stage_m upper_stage_m n_gaugings gauged_min_stage_m
#>    <int>         <num>         <num>      <int>              <num>
#> 1:     1           0.5           2.5         41                0.5
#>    gauged_max_stage_m lower_unsupported_m upper_unsupported_m
#>                 <num>               <num>               <num>
#> 1:                2.5                   0                   0
#>    lower_unsupported_frac upper_unsupported_frac
#>                     <num>                  <num>
#> 1:                      0                      0
